segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then after fourteen years I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus along as well.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I went up in response to a revelation, and I laid before them the good news that I proclaim among the Gentiles—though privately, before those of repute—for fear that I might be running, or had run, in vain.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But not even Titus, who was with me, though he was a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But because of the false brothers smuggled in, who slipped in to spy on the freedom we have in Christ Jesus so that they might enslave us—

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: to them we did not yield in submission even for a moment, so that the truth of the good news might remain with you.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As for those reputed to be something—whatever they were makes no difference to me; God shows no partiality—those of repute added nothing to me.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: On the contrary, when they saw that I had been entrusted with the good news for the uncircumcised, just as Peter had been for the circumcised

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: (for the one who worked through Peter for an apostleship to the circumcised worked through me also for the Gentiles),

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and when they recognized the grace given to me, James and Cephas and John, those reputed to be pillars, gave me and Barnabas the right hand of partnership, so that we should go to the Gentiles and they to the circumcised.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Only, we were to remember the poor—the very thing I was also eager to do.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But when Cephas came to Antioch, I opposed him to his face, because he stood condemned.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For before certain people came from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles; but when they came, he began to draw back and separate himself, fearing those of the circumcision.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the rest of the Jews joined him in this hypocrisy, so that even Barnabas was carried away by their hypocrisy.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But when I saw that they were not walking straight in line with the truth of the good news, I said to Cephas in front of everyone,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “If you, though a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how can you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: We are Jews by birth and not sinners from among the Gentiles;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: yet, knowing that a person is not justified by works of the law but only through faith in Jesus Christ, we too believed in Christ Jesus, so that we might be justified by faith in Christ and not by works of the law, because by works of the law no flesh will be justified.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But if, while seeking to be justified in Christ, we ourselves were also found to be sinners, is Christ then a servant of sin? Certainly not!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For if I build up again the very things I tore down, I show myself to be a transgressor.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For through the law I died to the law, so that I might live to God. I have been crucified with Christ;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. And the life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself up for me.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I do not set aside the grace of God; for if righteousness comes through the law, then Christ died for nothing.

notes.note: The Greek word was an ordinary term for the announcement of good news, used also of public and imperial proclamations. 'Gospel' now sounds like a religious term or a book title, so the plain meaning is given. Many modern translations alternate between 'gospel' and 'good news'.

The Greek is the plural of the ordinary word for a people or nation; in Jewish usage 'the nations' meant the non-Jewish peoples. This translation renders it 'Gentiles' in that sense and 'nations' where peoples as such are meant, but it is one Greek word throughout.

notes.phrase: because of the false brothers smuggled in
notes.note: Paul's sentence breaks off here and is never grammatically completed; the Greek has no main verb. Some translations supply one ('this matter arose because of...'), making the false brothers the cause of the dispute over Titus; others attach the clause to verse 3 or to verse 5. The translation leaves the break as Paul wrote it.

Literally 'God does not receive a person's face', a Hebrew idiom that entered Greek through the Septuagint. It means favoring someone because of status or appearance. The literal form would not be understood in English, so the sense is given.

Cephas is the Aramaic form of the name whose Greek equivalent is Peter; both mean 'rock'. Paul uses both forms in this chapter for the same man, and the translation keeps whichever the Greek has in each verse.

The Greek word denotes sharing or joint participation in a common undertaking, and a handshake sealing an agreed division of work suits that sense. 'Fellowship' now suggests friendly association more than a working agreement. Most translations keep 'fellowship'.

Literally 'those from circumcision'. The phrase may mean Jewish believers who insisted that Gentile converts be circumcised, or Jews more generally, whether believers or not. It is also unclear whether they are the same people as those who came from James; the translation leaves the phrase open.

notes.phrase: how can you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?
notes.note: Ancient manuscripts have no quotation marks, and it is disputed where Paul's words to Cephas end. The translation closes the speech here, as most recent versions do. Others carry it through verse 21, and it may be that Paul's report of what he said passes gradually into argument addressed to the Galatians.

Greek has one word-family where English has two: the verb 'justify' here belongs with the noun rendered 'righteousness' in verse 21 and with the adjective 'righteous' or 'just'. To be justified is to be declared or shown to be in the right. Some scholars prefer 'justice' vocabulary throughout to keep the link visible in English.

The Greek is literally 'faith of Jesus Christ'. It can mean either faith in Jesus Christ or the faithfulness of Jesus Christ, that is, his own faithful obedience. The translation follows the traditional and still majority reading, but the other has substantial scholarly support. The same applies to 'faith in Christ' later in the verse.

The phrase means deeds done in obedience to the law of Moses. Scholars dispute whether Paul means law-observance in general or especially the practices that marked Jews off from Gentiles, such as circumcision, food rules and the Sabbath. Circumcision and shared meals are the issues in this chapter.

notes.phrase: faith in the Son of God
notes.traditional: faith in the Son of God
notes.note: As in verse 16, the Greek is literally 'faith of the Son of God'. It may instead mean 'the faithfulness of the Son of God', his own faithfulness shown in giving himself up. The majority reading is followed here; the alternative has substantial scholarly support.

candidates.reason: Recurs across Paul, Acts and 1 John, where translators vary between fellowship, partnership, sharing and participation, and the choice shapes how readers hear it.
Ranges from the physical body to humanity to the sphere opposed to the Spirit, and versions that paraphrase it ('sinful nature', 'human being') hide the repetition.
Pervasive in the letters; 'grace', 'favor' and 'gift' are all defensible, and a single policy is needed.
Needs a consistent policy on 'law', 'the law' or 'Law', especially where the Greek lacks the article, as in 'works of the law'.
Used both for the rite and as a collective for Jews (with ἀκροβυστία for Gentiles); the abstract-for-group usage needs one consistent treatment.

warnings: Verse 7: πιστεύω is not rendered with a register form (believe / trust) and has no register-exception note.

patch.reason: euangelion promoted to active after full-run drift (good news 37 / gospel 35)
